tooltip.help.shift.adder:
§bExact inverse of the §aRedstone Comparator§b.

In '§6Compare§b' mode, it will test if the §aback signal§b is less than or equal to the §ahighest side signal§b ( §a<=§b ).

In '§6Add§b' mode, it will add the §aback signal§b to the §ahighest side signal§b (up to §c15§b).§r

tooltip.help.shift.analog_cell:
§bMemory cell that can store an analog signal.

In '§6Set§b' mode, it will constantly update and store the §aback signal§b as long as there is a §asignal provided on the side§b.

In '§6Reset§b' mode, it will constantly update and store the §aback signal§b (if greater than §c0§b). Any §asignal supplied on the side§b will reset output to §c0§b.§r
tooltip.help.shift.better_comparator: §bA glorified §aVanilla Comparator§b which works on §91 tick pulses§b. The §asides§b can read signals from even more sources (example: a lever).§r
tooltip.help.shift.checker:
§bIn '§6Equal§b' mode, it checks if the §aback signal§b is §aexactly equal§b to the §ahighest side signal§b. 

In '§6Different§b' mode, it checks if the §atwo signals§b are different from one another.

§aAlways outputs the same signal strength received from back signal with successful check.§r
tooltip.help.shift.delayer:
§bDelays the §ainput signal§b by §91, 2, 3, or 4 ticks§b, without changing the §cstrength§b or length (§9duration§b) of the signal.

Has a §65th mode§b that will delay the §ainput signal§b using the §ahighest side signal§b ( §9+1§b ).§r
tooltip.help.shift.demuxer:
§bChecks for bit §c1, 2, 4, or 8§b from the §aback signal§b.

Has a §65th mode§b where the tested bit is selected by the §ahighest side signal§b (§c1§b-> bit 1, §c2§b-> bit 2, §c3§b-> bit 4, §c4§b-> bit 8).§r
tooltip.help.shift.edge_detector:
§bIn '§6Rising Edge§b' mode, it emits a §91-tick pulse§b when the §aback signal§b is increased.

In '§6Falling Edge§b' mode, it emits a §91-tick pulse§b when the §aback signal§b is decreased.§r
tooltip.help.shift.shifter:
§bIn '§6Shift Up§b' mode, it shifts any bit(s) up by the §ahighest side signal§b.

In '§6Shift Down§b' mode, it shifts any bit(s) down by the §ahighest side signal§b.

Example: In '§6Shift Up§b' mode, with a §aside signal§b of §c1§b, the §aback signal§b of §c6§b would output §c12§b.§r
tooltip.help.shift.signal_generator:
§bGenerates a signal sequentially §9every tick§b.

§6Sequence§b will only advance while §apowered (from the back§b).

In '§6Saw§b', '§6Inverted Saw§b', '§6Triangle§b' and '§6Random§b' mode, the §aoutput signal§b will be between §c0-15§b while not powered from the sides.
If §apowered from the sides§b, the signal will stay within a set range (§abetween the lowest side signal and highest side signal, inclusive§b).

In '§6Square§b' mode, the time between oscillation will be equal to the §ahighest side signal §9+ 1 tick§b.

In '§6Sine§b' mode, the number of degrees §9per tick§b is equal to the §ahighest side§b signal §c+ 1§b.§r
tooltip.help.shift.analog_redstone_torch: §bWorks just like a normal redstone torch but can have a specific §aoutput value§b set.§r
tooltip.help.shift.analog_button: §bWorks just like a normal stone button but can have a specific §aoutput value§b set.§r
tooltip.help.shift.analog_lever: §bWorks just like a normal lever but can have a specific §aoutput value§b set.§r
tooltip.help.shift.analog_redstone_block: §bWorks just like a normal redstone block §a(can be moved)§b but can have a specific §aoutput value§b set.§r
tooltip.help.shift.analog_redstone_lamp: §bWorks just like a normal redstone lamp but with §evariable light levels§b relative to the §credstone signal §areceived§b.§r
tooltip.help.shift.analog_jukebox: §bThis jukebox has an §6inventory§b consisting of 15 spaces for music discs only. Depending on the §credstone signal §areceived§b, it will play a different music disc.§r
tooltip.help.shift.instrument_swapper_bl: §bUsed to hot-swap noteblock §6instrument§b without replacing a block. Has an §6inventory§b consisting of 16 spaces, you can place any block or head that has a specific instrument or sound for noteblocks in those slots. §cSignal strength§b determines which inventory slot is used (§c0-15§b).§r
tooltip.help.shift.analog_note_block:
§bThis note block plays a §fsound§b with the pitch dependent on the §csignal strength§b.

§aRight-clicking§b the block will switch between ranges '§6high§b' and '§6low§b'.§r
tooltip.help.shift.enriched_redstone:
§bThis redstone dust is mixed with conductive metals to improve §aefficiency§b and transport §adistance§b.

Loses §cone signal strength§b every §f4 blocks§b instead of every §f1 block§b.§r
tooltip.help.shift.perfected_redstone:
§bThis redstone dust is an alloy of conductive materials, resulting in incredible efficiency.

§cComplete signal strength retention§b (§fup to 32 blocks§b).§r
tooltip.help.shift.keyboard_item:
§bThe Keyboard allows you to remotely power §aResonant Gates§b using §akeybinds or MIDI input§b (use the §credstone button§b in the top right of the menu to configure MIDI device).

The menu allows you to §abind each key individually to any network§b and chose the §cpower emitted§b when the key is pressed (if the power selected is '§c?§b', then the signal will be 15 for keyboard, and between 1 and 15 for MIDI input, based on §9velocity of the keypress§b)
tooltip.help.shift.sequencer_record:
§bBy burning a disc, you erased it's sounds and made it malleable enough to transfer data from sequencer to sequencer.

It's still usable in a Jukebox, but only produces weird noises.
tooltip.help.shift.analog_dispenser_bloc:
§bDispenser that only §fshoots§b when §apowered in the back§b, with §fspeed§b scaled by the §cstrength§b of the back input

you can aim by §cpowering the sides§b (powering a side will shoot in the §aopposite direction§b)

example: aimed at the sky, you will have to power it from the bottom, and to shoot to the east you'd power from the west (otherwise it would shoot straight up).
tooltip.help.shift.sequencer:
§bThe Sequencer is a diode capable of emitting §9sequences§b of §credstone pulse/signals§b with 3 §6modes§b:

'§6play§b': play the selected sequence once per §csignal change§b

'§6repeat§b': repeat the selected sequence while §cpowered§b

'§6record§b': record the §csignal received§b and store it as a new sequence

for more details, use the help in the top right corner of the Sequencer menu
tooltip.help.shift.redstone_booster: §bUse on blocks to boost them. The boosted blocks run as fast as they can (§91 game tick§b instead of §c1 redstone tick§b, aka §92 game ticks§b). Might cause visual glitches, but signals emitted in 1 game tick pulses do work with redstone wires (Vanilla or from this mod).
tooltip.help.shift.pixel_block:
§bBlock that changes §fcolor§b based on §cinput received§b.

Use the §asame palette order as wool/terracotta§b, with the exception of black being emitted for §cpower 0§b and white at §cpower 15§b.

Does not transmit redstone (will not bleed it's colors to neighboring pixels if directly powered).
tooltip.help.shift.programmable_gate:
§bThis diode will emit §csignals§b using a '§ftruth table§b' of §csignals§b

the §csignal§b is selected by using the §aback signal§b as the §fcolumn§b and the §astrongest side signal§b as the §frow§b

you can load §apresets§b using the top right button in the menu, and copy the settings to another programmable gate by §5[%3$s§5]§b with the configured programmable gate (will be copied from the item to the block)
tooltip.help.shift.resonant_gate: §bGate that can link to other §fresonant gate§b and §fkeyboards§b in a §anamed network§b, the §csignal received§b in the back will be §cemitted§b by all gates' (including the one powered) front instantly (§ano range or dimension restriction§b).
tooltip.help.ctrl.keyboard_item:
§5[%2$s§5]§b + §5[%1$s§5]§b to open the menu, §5[%1$s§5]§b to activate (§athe redstone button will light up§b) and all matching keybinds will be caught by the Keyboard, §5[%1$s§5]§b again to disable

It doesn't need to stay in your hand to work once activated (need to be in your inventory though).
tooltip.help.ctrl.sequencer_record: §5[%1$s§5]§b a sequencer to copy it's data to the record, §5[%2$s§5]§b + §5[%1$s§5]§b a sequencer to override it's data with the record's. §5[%1$s§5]§b the air to copy the data to your clip board, §5[%2$s§5]§b + §5[%1$s§5]§b the air to load data from your clip board.
tooltip.help.ctrl.sequencer:
§5[%1$s§5]§b to open the screen, §5[%2$s§5]§b + §5[%1$s§5]§b to cycle §6modes§b.

%9$s

screen.arss.sequencer.help:
§5Middle Click§r: set §7length§r to §lcursor§r (§5+Ctrl§r: toggle §alimit§r)
§5Left Click§r: move §bhead§r to §lcursor§r (§5+Ctrl§r: copy current §bhead§r §cpower§r to new §bhead§r position, §5+Shift§r: §9select§r while moving)
§5Right Click§r: set §cpower§r under §lcursor§r
§5Up/Down§r: increase/decrease §cpower§r at §bhead§r/§9selection§r.
§5Left/Right§r: move §bhead§r left/right or whole §9selection§r (§5+Ctrl§r: also copy §cpower§r)
§5Left/Right + Shift§r: §9select§r and move §bhead§r (instead of moving §9selection§r)
§5Home/End§r: move §bhead§r to first tick or last tick (§5+Ctrl§r: also copy §cpower§r, §5+Shift§r: also §9select§r)
§5Page Up/Down§r: move view by a full screen backward/forward (50 ticks)
§5Scroll Up/Down§r: move view by 10 ticks
§5Ctrl + C/X§r: copy/cut §9selection§r to internal clip board
§5Ctrl + V§r: paste §9selection§r to the §bhead§r (moving the §bhead§r right in the process)§r
§5Space§r: Play/Pause
screen.arss.sequencer_help.chapter.0:
§bMouse§r
§b- Left click:§r move the head.
§b- Right click:§r set power.
§b- Middle click:§r set length
    §a+ Ctrl:§r toggle limit/sub-sequence.
§b- Scroll Up/Down:§r move the view
    (without moving the head) to
    the next/previous ticks.

§bKeyboard§r
§b- Space:§r toggle playback
    (as if the sequencer was
    powered/unpowered).
§b- Left/Right:§r Move the head
    (or selected area)
    forward/backward.
§b- Up/Down:§r increase/decrease the
    power at the §bhead§r or §bselection§r.
   §a+ Shift:§r steps of 5.
   §a+ Ctrl:§r maximum/minimum (15/0).
§b- Home/End:§r move the head to
    the start/end of the sequence.
§b- Ctrl + head/selection moving:§r clone
    power at new head/selection
    location.
§b- Shift + Head moving:§r selection.
§b- Escape:§r Cancel selection.
§b- Ctrl + C:§r copy selection.
§b- Ctrl + V:§r paste selection at head
    position (and only at head position,
    will not replace a selection).

screen.arss.sequencer_help.chapter.1:
§c§lRed§r: redstone power

§b§lBlue§r: head/tick

§7§lGray:§r end

§a§lGreen§r: limits/sub-sequences

§e§lYellow§r: Head and cursor information (where they are in the sequence in tick and what power will be emitted)

§lButtons§r: set how the sides of the sequencer will be used.
screen.arss.sequencer_help.chapter.2:
The length (§7dark grey line§f) is where the sequence finishes (aka stop in §6Play Once§f mode, or repeat in §6Loop§f mode).

To set the §7length§f, use §bmiddle click§f.
You can also set limits/boundaries (§agreen lines§f) in the sequence (toggle via §bmiddle click + ctrl§f).

The first §btick§f, §alimits§f and the §7length§f (aka last tick or end) have values above them, equal to the power require to use those limits.


For more info on §aLimits§f, see '§lPlay§r§f' chapter.
screen.arss.sequencer_help.chapter.3:
The head (§blight blue line§f) is where the sequencer is currently reading the power.

When §6playing§f, the §bhead§f will automatically move right every tick.

To move the head, use §bleft click or the arrow keys§f (left/right).

While moving the head, you can hold the §bCtrl§f key to copy the power and the §bShift§f key to select an area.
screen.arss.sequencer_help.chapter.4:
The power can be set in two ways, either with §bright-click and/or up/down keys§f, or recorded using the §6record mode§f.

In §6record mode§f, if you power a §lstart/finish side§r (left/right by default), then the §lrecord side§r (back by default) will be copied to the sequencer and the §bhead§f will advance by 1 tick.
screen.arss.sequencer_help.chapter.5:
While moving the §bhead§f, you can §bhold Shift§f to select an area. Once an area is selected, moving the §bhead§f with the §barrow keys§f (left/right) will instead move the selection left/right.

§bCtrl + C§f will copy the selection to an internal clipboard,

§bCtrl + X§f will cut (same as copy, but will also reset the power in the selection).

§bCtrl + V§f will paste the last copy/cut to the §bhead§f, moving it to the right in the process.
screen.arss.sequencer_help.chapter.6:
You can test a sequence by pressing §bSpace§f to toggle §cplay§f mode (as if it was powered).
If you have defined §alimits§f (see 'Length' chapter), and set the §linputs§r (bottom buttons named 'start' and 'finish'), then the sequence played will be between the §astart limit§f and §afinish limit§f.

Example: '§lstart§r' is 1 and '§lfinish§r' is 2, we set a §alimit§f on tick 10, the sequence played will be between tick 0 and tick 10.

If we power '§lstart§r' with a signal of 2 and '§lend§r' with 15 or 0, then every ticks from 10 to §7length§f will be played.
